Blue-cheeked Bee-eater

निळ्या गालाचा वेडा राघू

Merops persicus

The Blue-cheeked Bee-eater is a graceful green bird with a dark eye stripe bordered by blue. Its long wings, slender bill and extended central tail feathers make it especially elegant when it leaves a perch to catch an insect in flight.

About the bird

How to recognise the Blue-cheeked Bee-eater

Most of the body is green, with blue around the dark eye mask and a yellow throat that gives way to a warmer rufous patch below. Adult birds have long central tail feathers, while younger birds have a shorter-looking tail.

Several bee-eaters share similar colours. The face pattern, throat colours and overall size are useful features to compare rather than relying on the green plumage alone.

Natural habitat

The places where it lives

It favours open country, including dry plains, farmland and scrub, often with water nearby. Scattered trees, wires and exposed branches provide convenient places to perch between feeding flights.

Sandy ground and banks are important where the birds breed. Like other bee-eaters, they nest in tunnels excavated in suitable earth.

Food habits

What it eats and how it feeds

Its food consists of flying insects, including bees, wasps, dragonflies and other insects caught in the air. The bird often launches from a perch, catches its prey and returns to a resting place.

It handles some insects against a perch before swallowing them. Feeding activity depends on the insects available around the site.

Where it occurs in India

Where you may find it in India

In India, the Blue-cheeked Bee-eater is particularly associated with the northwest, including Gujarat and Rajasthan. Breeding birds and summer visitors use suitable open landscapes in this region.

It is more local elsewhere, and birds may be recorded beyond the main breeding areas during movement.
